finding.claim: Gateway logged a completed HTTP 200 request at 12:00:00Z and backend logged 'Request processing exceeded deadline' at 12:00:14Z, placing the first observed error 14 seconds after the gateway success; the backend deadline breach localizes the visible symptom to backend request processing, but the excerpt names no downstream dependency and carries no saturation or connection-failure signature, so a causal mechanism is not yet observed.

requested_checks.question: Re-query backend logs across the full window without a severity filter to recover any pool wait/timeout, thread-exhaustion, or dependency connection-failure lines that ERROR-only filtering may hide.
requested_checks.reason: Public logs may lack severity metadata, so the earlier ERROR-only query can hide the saturation or dependency signatures needed to discriminate; a severity-free backend sweep is the cheapest discriminating source still allowed.
requested_checks.expected_discriminator: Pool wait/timeout or thread-exhaustion signatures localize to backend_resource_saturation or backend_pool_config_regression; redis connection failures or timeouts surfacing during backend handling localize to redis_unavailable, and their order relative to 12:00:14Z establishes which side failed first.

requested_checks.question: Sweep gateway logs across the window without a severity filter to establish the earliest error chronology and request-outcome sequence relative to the backend deadline breach at 12:00:14Z.
requested_checks.reason: Gateway is the entry point where the user-visible symptom appears; its chronology around the single observed HTTP 200 establishes whether the first failure is backend-local or a propagated dependency effect, complementing the backend sweep.
requested_checks.expected_discriminator: Gateway errors beginning only after backend timeouts indicate a backend-origin failure, while gateway errors that precede or coincide with backend dependency-connection failures point to a dependency-origin cause.
